
Randomizing the treatment does not remove mediator-outcome confounding. `pmed_sensitivity()`
reports how a specified additive bias $b$ in the mean-based indirect effect changes the
share $(\text{indirect} + b) / \text{total}$, holding the total effect fixed. In the gauge and
incremental frameworks, this perturbation represents bias in the cross-world mean when their
assumption A4 (no exposure-induced mediator-outcome confounding) fails.

**Scope.** The bias grid is a sensitivity analysis for the gauge and incremental shares. The
tie-adjusted probability from `pmed()` and the manuscript's A2/A5 sensitivity analyses are
outside its scope. A Sobol variance share would require a separately specified perturbation
of its variance component.

## From components

If you have an indirect and a total effect from any source:

```{r}
library(probmed)
pmed_sensitivity(indirect = 0.30, total = 0.50, threshold = 0, evalue = TRUE)
```

The printed result gives the tipping bias that drives the indirect effect to zero and the bias
that drives the share to `threshold`. With `evalue = TRUE` it adds a coarse E-value, which needs the
suggested package EValue; `se` (the standard error of `indirect`) is used only for the E-value's
interval bound.

## From a fitted object

```{r}
fit <- ward_residual(data.frame(A, M, Y, C))
pmed_sensitivity(fit, threshold = 0)
```

The default grid spans plus and minus the absolute indirect effect in 11 points; pass `bias_grid`
to change it. The share can leave [0, 1] on the grid. That signals an implausibly large bias, not
a valid share.

## Incremental version

`incr_sensitivity()` gives the same tipping analysis per shift value delta for `incr_pmed()`.
See [Incremental P_med](incremental-pmed.html).

## Reading the result

1. Pick a threshold that matters substantively (zero is the usual one).
2. Compare the tipping bias to the size of covariate effects you can name. A tipping bias
   larger than any measured confounder is evidence of robustness; a smaller one is not.
3. Report the E-value, if used, as a coarse summary, not as a test.

This analysis addresses M-Y confounding only. It does not address treatment-mediator
confounding, measurement error, or the boundary behavior described in
[Modern estimands](modern-estimands.html#boundary-behavior).
